inputs.original_text: Earlier this month, an Indiana judge blocked a prolife law, arguing that limiting abortion violates freedom of religion. The claim, brought by the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice, argued that an Indiana law “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” Judge Christina R. [...] The post This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right appeared first on LifeNews.com .
inputs.modified_text: This is a carefully packaged maneuver: turn abortion access into a religious-liberty dispute, then let the language of “neutral” rights obscure what the ruling does to the prolife law. The ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice made the claim, and the judge blocked the law. That framing is the point—it gives institutions a respectable cover while shifting attention away from the underlying fight. The blunt title, “This Judge Thinks Killing Babies in Abortions is a Religious Right,” may be provocative, but the larger concern is who benefits when courts redefine the issue this way.
